mappings.note: Who made the lac bangles -- locating a stated detail in the story; not C-HIN1.1-LO-1, which is about discussing a text rather than retrieving a point from it.
What kind of bangles Badlu made -- the craft's own product vocabulary (laakh); C-HIN2.1-LO-1 would treat a handicraft term as a plot point.
Who Badlu was -- character identification, the analysis LO; not C-HIN1.2-LO-2, no social value is at issue.
When the narrator usually met Badlu -- sequence/detail in the narrative, not craft vocabulary.
Daily output of bangles -- a fact about the craft's practice, so the handicraft-language LO rather than the generic text-detail LO.
How the bangles on the roller looked to Badlu -- the rainbow image, i.e. appreciating the writer's shilp; not C-HIN2.1-LO-1, which would reduce a simile to a fact.
Effect of the father's transfer on the narrator -- cause and effect inside the narrative.
Who Rajjo was -- character identification.
Where Badlu lived -- setting detail; not the craft LO, the village is not a craft term.
Why the narrator called him 'Badlu kaka' -- a kinship term extended to a non-kin artisan, which is the story's social value; C-HIN2.1-LO-1 would miss that the question asks why, socially.
Where he sat to work (the machiya) -- the craftsman's workplace register, not a plot detail.
What he melted in the furnace -- craft material and process vocabulary.
What material he used for lac bangles -- craft material; the handicraft LO is the only one naming hastakala.
How he made lac bangles -- the technique itself, the clearest case for the handicraft-language LO.
What work he did sitting on the machiya -- craft practice, paired with q116429.
Where the narrator spent most of his village time -- narrative detail, not craft technique.
What Badlu called the narrator -- a stated detail; unlike q116428 it asks what, not why, so no social-value LO.
Where Badlu seated the narrator -- stated detail.
Duplicate stem of q116424 (rainbow image on the roller) -- same shilp-appreciation outcome.
What Badlu was -- identity/occupation as stated; the craft LO is reserved for questions about the craft's materials and technique.
His hereditary trade -- paitrik pesha is craft-community vocabulary, so the handicraft LO.
How he sold the bangles (barter for grain) -- the craft's trade practice, not a generic plot fact.
Where his bangles were consumed -- the craft's market; grouped with the other craft-practice items.
What he insisted on at weddings -- a reeti-riwaz whose social meaning is the point; C-HIN1.2-LO-1 is about the pupil asking such questions, not answering one.
Which pratyay is used in 'paitrik' -- word-formation grammar, so the language-system LO; C-HIN2.1-LO-2 covers idioms and proverbs, not affixes.
Why the narrator could not visit for a long spell -- an inference from the narrative.
Where he went in the summer holidays -- stated detail.
What had changed after 8-10 years -- machine bangles displacing the artisan, the story's social value; C-HIN3.2-LO-1 would make the decline of a livelihood a craft-vocabulary item.
What had become of the uncle's younger daughter -- narrative detail.
Where he found Badlu -- setting detail on the return visit.
Antonym of 'bahudha' -- word meaning, which is the shabd/muhavra LO; not C-HIN4.1-LO-1, no grammatical form is being tested.
Duplicate stem of q116426 (who Rajjo was) -- same character-identification outcome.
How many mangoes Rajjo brought -- stated detail.
What sort of bangles Rajjo wore -- a stated detail about a character; unlike q116420 the bangles are glass, not the craft's own product.
When Badlu made his last pair -- the plot's turning point as a locatable fact, not the social reading of it.
Place of articulation of pa, pha, ba, bha, ma -- phonology, part of the written language system LO.
Kinds of antahstha consonants -- varna classification, grammar not vocabulary.
Adjective derived from a noun -- word-class grammar.
Adjective derived from a noun (duplicate stem _1) -- same grammar outcome.
Which word is NOT a noun-derived adjective (_2) -- same word-class grammar.
Which word is NOT a noun-derived adjective (_3) -- same word-class grammar.
Adjective derived from a noun (_4) -- same word-class grammar.
Adjective derived from a pronoun -- word-class grammar.
Which word is NOT a verb-derived adjective -- word-class grammar.
Adjective derived from a verb -- word-class grammar.
Feminine formed from a masculine -- ling, a grammatical form.
Which word is tadbhav from Sanskrit -- word-origin classification, part of the language system.
Place of articulation of ta-varga -- phonology.
Place of articulation of pa-varga -- phonology.
Place of articulation of cha-varga -- phonology.
What a group of varnas is called -- metalanguage of grammar.
What kind of consonants ksh, tra, gya are -- varna classification.
Classifying 'pustak' by origin (tatsam/tadbhav/deshaj/videshi) -- grammar, not word meaning.
Classifying 'aag' by origin -- same word-origin grammar.
Classifying 'prithvi' by origin -- same word-origin grammar.
Classifying 'tebul' by origin (videshi) -- same word-origin grammar.
Classifying 'naak' by origin -- same word-origin grammar.
